groups.title: Flexbox
groups.question: You are building a navigation bar where items sit in a row, one item should take up the leftover space, and long text keeps overflowing. Explain how flexbox handles this.

followUps.Main axis and cross axis: You switch flex-direction to column and justify-content now moves things vertically. Why?
followUps.flex-grow, shrink and basis: A flex item with long text refuses to shrink and overflows. What is happening and how do you fix it?

evidence.text: Flexbox lays items along a main axis and aligns them on a cross axis.
justify-content works along the main axis and align-items along the cross axis.
Changing the direction to column swaps which way the main axis runs, so the two properties swap effect.

notEnough: Only saying justify is horizontal and align is vertical.

evidence.text: flex-grow decides how free space is shared, flex-shrink how items give up space, and flex-basis the starting size.
flex: 1 makes items share the available space evenly.
Flex items will not shrink below their content size by default, and setting min-width to 0 lets them shrink.

notEnough: Only listing the three properties without saying what each controls.

groups.title: Grid
groups.question: You need a page layout with a header, sidebar and main area, plus a product grid that adds columns on wider screens. Explain how CSS Grid handles both.

followUps.Tracks and areas: When would you choose grid over flexbox for a layout?
followUps.auto-fit, minmax and fr: How does a grid add or remove columns as the screen gets wider, without media queries?

evidence.text: Grid controls rows and columns at the same time, while flexbox works in one direction.
Items can be placed by line numbers or by named areas, which makes page layouts readable.
Grid suits whole-page layouts and anything arranged in rows and columns.

notEnough: Only saying grid is for two dimensions without an example of when it helps.

evidence.text: minmax sets a minimum and maximum size for each column.
auto-fit fits as many columns as there is room for at that minimum size.
The fr unit shares leftover space between columns, so they stretch to fill the row.

notEnough: Only reciting the repeat auto-fit minmax line without explaining what each part does.

groups.title: Responsive Design
groups.question: Your site looks fine on your laptop but is cramped on phones, and buttons are hard to tap. Explain how you would make it responsive.

followUps.Mobile-first and media queries: Why start with the mobile layout and add styles for larger screens, instead of the other way round?
followUps.The viewport and touch targets: Why can a menu that opens on hover be a problem on phones?

evidence.text: Mobile-first starts with the simplest small-screen layout and adds complexity with min-width media queries.
Breakpoints should be placed where the content starts to look broken, not at specific device sizes.
Building up from small screens usually means less CSS to undo than shrinking a desktop design.

notEnough: Only saying media queries change styles at screen sizes.

evidence.text: The viewport meta tag makes mobile browsers use the device width instead of pretending to be a desktop.
Buttons and links need to be big enough to tap with a finger without hitting the wrong one.
Touch screens have no hover, so anything that only appears on hover can be unreachable.

notEnough: Only saying the site should work on mobile without naming what breaks.

groups.title: Modern Layout
groups.question: A product card is used both in a narrow sidebar and in a wide main column, and your site will also be translated to Arabic, which reads right to left. Explain how modern CSS handles both.

followUps.Container queries: Why can't a media query alone make the same card look right in both the sidebar and the main column?
followUps.Logical properties and intrinsic sizing: How do logical properties help when the page switches to a right-to-left language?

evidence.text: Media queries respond to the size of the whole screen, not the space a component actually has.
Container queries style a component based on the size of its parent container.
That lets the same component adapt wherever it is placed.

notEnough: Only saying container queries are newer media queries.

evidence.text: Logical properties like margin-inline-start follow the writing direction instead of a fixed left or right.
In a right-to-left language, they flip automatically without separate CSS.
Intrinsic sizing keywords like min-content and fit-content let an element size itself to its content.

notEnough: Only saying logical properties are the new names for margins.
